verified.title: Player death followed by a boss kill runs both flow.defeat and flow.victory

verdicts.evidence: ArenaScene.ts:1419-1431 playerDied sets ending='defeat', does not call arsenal.clearAll, and schedules flow.defeat() at 1300ms. update() (line 1040) still calls updateEnemy for all non-dying enemies, with dt=0 but absolute `now`. enemies.ts:145-156 calls tickBurn/tickPoison (systems/combat.ts:27-33, time-based, not dt-based) and then scene.damageEnemy(e, burn, null, {isDot:true}). damageEnemy (line 666) has only an `!e.alive` guard, no ending/phase guard. killEnemy with credit=true reaches line 873 `if (e === this.boss) this.bossDefeated()`. bossDefeated (line 1392) has no `if (this.ending) return` guard. It sets ending='victory' and schedules flow.victory() at 2200ms. flow.victory/defeat (flow.ts:205-257) have no phase guard and both call finish(), which calls submitRun and recordRun again (non-lab, non-overtime), so the profile is written twice. arsenal.update (line 1050) also keeps running after death, so shots, puddles and pots can finish the boss too. The only thing that stops it is the player restarting the scene before the 2.2s victory timer fires.
verdicts.correction: Severity is overstated. The profile is double-counted (two recorded runs, one loss and one win, doubled kills and coins, boss clear credited on a lost run), but the save is not corrupted and nothing crashes or softlocks. The trigger is a narrow window: the boss must die from a burn or poison tick or an in-flight shot or puddle after the player has died, and the player must not restart before the 2.2s victory timer fires. I rate it high (wrong rule plus stat inflation). The "Keep going" overtime consequence follows from the victory card replacing the defeat card, but I did not trace the overtime path in detail.

verified.title: Pickpocket loot vanishes whenever the Pickpocket dies without kill credit

verdicts.evidence:

verdicts.correction: Minor: the loss is limited to Pickpocket elites alive at wave end (loot coins at 1 each). The "worse during stagger" part rests on affixTick running with dt=0, which I read but did not run. Severity high is defensible but is on the lower side of high, since the amount is small coins per elite.

verdicts.evidence:
The cited code matches the source as it stands today. src/scenes/ArenaScene.ts:830 has `if (!credit) return;`, and that line comes before the Pickpocket loot loop at :854 (`for (let i = 0; i < e.loot; i++) this.dropCoin(...)`).
The trigger happens in real runs. At :1035, beginCheckout() fires when `waveTime >= wave.duration` on any non-boss, non-mini, non-stockroom aisle, whether or not enemies are still alive. :1384 then kills every living enemy with killEnemy(e, false). miniDefeated (:514) and bossDefeated (:1411) also call killEnemy(e, false).
Pickpocket elites are normal spawns: createEnemy uses pickAffix (enemies.ts:99), and e.loot++ in affixTick (enemies.ts:312-316) is the only place loot is stored.
Nothing else drops or credits e.loot. The sweep at :1386 credits only coins still on the floor, and absorbCoin (:894-902) already set the absorbed coins to inactive.
Repro under vitest: with Phaser mocked and location/window/localStorage stubbed, I called the real ArenaScene.prototype.killEnemy on a stub scene, passing an enemy with loot=12 and affix=pickpocket and credit=false. The test passed with 0 dropCoin calls and e.alive=false. All 12 coins were lost.
The stagger detail also holds: :1040 calls updateEnemy with dt=0 during checkout, and affixTick (enemies.ts:162) is gated only on state!=='spawn'. absorbCoin does not depend on dt, so a stationary Pickpocket keeps absorbing coins that are in its radius and on the ground (z<=4).

verdicts.correction:
I would rate this medium, not high. It only happens when a Pickpocket elite, which is just one of the five elite affixes, is still alive at aisle end, a mini-boss kill or a boss kill. The loss is limited to the coins it absorbed, and a player is unlikely to notice them missing. It is a silent currency leak, not a rule players run into regularly.
The stagger part is overstated. With dt=0 the Pickpocket can't move. During checkout, no-credit kills don't drop coins, and absorbCoin skips coins that are airborne (z>4) or being pulled. So the only coins it can pick up during the stagger are ones already on the ground within about 26 px plus its own radius. That window lasts at most 40 ms per enemy.
In miniDefeated and bossDefeated the kill happens synchronously, so there is no stagger at all. The loot is still lost on those paths, though.

verified.title: Every status timer runs on wall-clock time and keeps expiring through pause, blur and slow frames

verdicts.evidence:
src/scenes/phaserCtx.ts:31 now() = sc.time.now/1000, and ArenaScene.ts:559, 668, 1009, 1176 use time.now directly.
node_modules/phaser/src/time/Clock.js:358-362: update() sets this.now = time, and the scene Clock only updates while the scene runs.
src/flow.ts:266-280: pause() calls game.scene.pause('Arena'), so the clock freezes while the main loop keeps running. src/ui/ui.ts:149-150 wires window blur and visibilitychange to flow.pause('blur').
TimeStep.js:671/722: loop.time += rawDelta every frame. After a hidden tab, resume() calls resetDelta(), which sets time = performance.now(). Either way the first resumed frame sees a time jump equal to the pause length.
Absolute *Until timestamps (marks, slow, slide, blown) therefore expire across a pause. Nothing in the repo compensates; I found no pause-duration adjustment.
src/systems/combat.ts:27-33: tickBurn is capped at burnUntil, so the remaining burn ticks all fire in one frame on resume.
verdicts.correction:
The core claim holds for the pause and blur path. Two overstatements:
- The burn catch-up burst conserves total damage. It is not extra damage, only a spike, and it can be a burst kill.
- The low-fps drift is speculative (inferred from the dt cap, not measured).
Severity is medium at most, leaning toward low-medium. The effect is a pause-dependent loss of timed buffs and debuffs. It is not a crash or softlock.

verified.title: Key and pad presses made during an ending window fire at the start of the next aisle

verdicts.evidence: src/ui/ui.ts:883 initKeyboard(active = phase==='combat' && !paused). keyboard.ts:14-17 latches presses whenever the predicate holds. It is not limited to Keep going, because the checkout sweep before every shop leaves stale presses too (the shop phase does not latch or clear them). The impact is small. A stale active press only wastes one charge, and a stale dash only moves the goblin once at aisle start. The player has to press the key during a roughly 2 s ending window. Nothing crashes and nothing is corrupted. Severity is low to medium, so I put it at low. The gamepad is confirmed by trace, not just plausible: gamepad.ts:126-127 queues and takePad* consumes only in updatePlayer.

verified.title: Starting a pointer drag while the gamepad holds an item leaves an orphan ghost on screen

verdicts.evidence:
src/ui/shop.ts:661-678 onPointerDown has no `drag` guard. The only reset it does is padOff() (998-1002), which clears padKey and the .pad-cur classes and never touches `drag`.
beginDrag (682) overwrites `drag` with ghost:null. The pad path shopPad.confirm (1044) calls startGhost (685-700), which appends a ghost to document.body and creates a hint.
After a pointer press on another item, onPointerUp (842-849) calls endDrag (836-840) on the NEW drag, so the old ghost element is never removed.
If the mouse moves 5px or more, startGhost runs again (749), overwrites `hint` and leaks that bubble too.
No other cleanup exists: grep finds no sweep for .ghost or .drag-hint elsewhere.
The 'change' handler (72) only re-renders root, and ghost/hint live in body.
The trigger is reachable: mixed pad and mouse input in a real shop.
verdicts.correction: The trace holds. Severity should be low rather than medium. It needs mixed pad and mouse input mid-hold, it is cosmetic, and no game state is corrupted. The report understates the leak slightly: a leaked drag-hint bubble can occur too. I did not verify the claim that the ghost stays for the rest of the session. I found no cleanup, but I did not check whether leaving the shop hides body-level elements. The cause is the missing `drag` guard in onPointerDown, so the suggested fix (cancel any existing drag first) is right.

verified.title: A key swap can hand Escape to loadout or rotate, and that action then goes dead; Escape itself can never be rebound

verdicts.evidence:
The cited code matches the report.
- keymap.ts:80-91: `rebind` swaps, so the displaced action gets the old key of the slot being bound.
- ui.ts:841-848: the bare `else if (e.key === 'Escape')` branch only does preventDefault and sits before the loadout check.
- shop.ts:87 and 89: the Escape drag-cancel runs before the rotate check.
- ui.ts:341: `listenKey` treats Escape as cancel, so Escape can never be bound.
Trace of the mechanism: DEFAULT_KEYS has pause ['Escape',''] and loadout ['Tab','']. Binding pause slot 0 to Tab (or to R for rotate) makes `rebind` hand 'Escape' to loadout (or rotate). Keyboard Escape then hits the no-op branch, so Tab-less loadout is unreachable from the keyboard. R-less rotate is cancelled by the drag Escape.
Rotate on a drag is dead from the keyboard. Escape-while-listening cancels, so Escape can't be rebound.
The report's exact repro does not work. Binding pause SLOT 1 (empty) to Tab gives old = '', so loadout becomes ['',''] and `rebind` returns ok:false with reason 'last' (keymap.ts:92). No swap happens.
Mitigations the report omitted: the player can bind loadout or rotate to another key via slot 2 or by rebinding. The swap note names the displaced action. Pad Y still works. "Goes dead" is only true until the player rebinds it. The "Reset controls" remedy is not the only recovery.
verdicts.correction: The repro is wrong: it is slot 0 (the Escape slot), not slot 1, that has to be rebound. Slot 1 is empty, so binding it to Tab is refused with 'last'. "Dead" overstates it: loadout and rotate can be rebound to any other key, and the Reset-only recovery claim is untrue. The defect is real but a rare, self-inflicted, recoverable edge case, so low rather than medium.

verified.title: setGains preview disagrees with the real set count when a cart holds two copies of a type (double packs)
verified.extra: A second auditor reported the same root cause in state-economy.md line 43 ('Set badge on a double pack promises +1 when a double of that type is already in the cart'); read that section too and check both scenarios.

verdicts.evidence:
src/data/sets.ts:42-52 (setGains) matches the cited code. Line 44 adds weightIn of the first copy per type. setCount (l.24-28) and setLevels (l.31-37) take Math.max per type. Line 46 lets a double offer of an already-seen type through, and line 48 then adds +1 without checking whether the owned copy is already a double.
Scenario B (state-economy): placed [bell(double), pricegun], double-bell offer. have=3, to=4, levelUp is true. setCount stays 3 after buying, so the level-up is false.
Scenario A (engine-combat): placed [bell, bell(double)], offer pricegun. The first bell gives weight 1, so have=1 and to=2. The real count is 2 going to 3. The from/to is off by one.
Reachable: buyOffer (state/run.ts:268-279) puts the item on the shelf with no auto-merge, so unmerged duplicates sit in the cart. Merging is a manual drag (run.ts:203-216, 219-222). Two copies of the same type at different tiers cannot merge at all, and legendaries do not merge either.
Doubles are rolled for real in rollOffers (systems/shop.ts:74, shopIndex>=2). Offers of already-owned types are allowed by the weighting, and the pool only excludes types already in the current offers.
The preview is used in the live UI at ui/shop.ts:224, 252 and 382. No guard blocks it.
verdicts.correction: Both reports are right, and they are the same root cause with two symptoms. Scenario A is the first-copy-weight bug. Scenario B is the missing already-a-double check. The impact is only a wrong badge or preview: the engine counting is correct and nothing breaks. The effect is cosmetic or misleading, so medium is the upper bound (low to medium). It needs a duplicate of a type in the cart, with at least one copy a double, and a shop at index 2 or later. The claim that the shop 'sells a level-up that never happens' is accurate, but the player only loses coins on a x1.5 pack. The suggested fix of diffing setCount(placed + hypothetical) against setCount(placed) is sound.

Two overstatements: the "stinks for good" fish text was not checked, and the Scoby example needs the Scoby to be in the cart or owned-aged, which was not shown. verified.title: The inspector's Combine button on a shelf item consumes the cart copy

verdicts.evidence:
src/ui/shop.ts:626-632 onContext: right-click on any .item[data-uid] sets selectedUid. Shelf items are rendered via itemEl (shop.ts:298), so they have data-uid. shop.ts:373 loc = findItem(...), which covers the shelf. verified.title: Adjacency hooks use the tier of the best copy anywhere in the cart, so Gold Star does not reach the Scoby

verdicts.evidence:
src/engine/hooks.ts:312-314: top = max over all copies of (tier+boost), so the owner's tier is the best copy anywhere in the cart. Line 323: that tier goes into the source. hooks.ts:277-279: tune = resolveTune(s.tune, s.tier) is computed once per source, and c.tune() returns it for every weapon. touching(uid) returns bare ItemInstance[] (hooks.ts:207, 279), with no effective tier.
(a) decaf.ts:19-21 checks c.touches(stats.uid), which is true if any copy touches that weapon. It then uses c.tune(), the best-copy tune. With a ★1 Decaf touching and a ★3 Decaf elsewhere, the weaken is 25% where 15% is expected. No guard or reset intervenes.
(b) scoby.ts:21 uses the raw p.tier ?? 1 and never adds tierBoostOf(...). Gold Star's boost is only applied in hookSourcesFor (hooks.ts:314) and in computeBuild's eff(), so a boosted Scoby gets the unboosted dps. The Gold Star lift is lost for the poison.

verified.title: Items that do not scale with tier are still offered at 2/3 stars and can be upgraded for coins
verified.extra: The mechanics auditor (mechanics.md) claims upgradeItem (src/state/run.ts:241) has no UI caller and that combine is the only way to level up. Settle whether a player can pay coins to upgrade at all, and adjust this claim accordingly.

verdicts.evidence:
Shop offers: src/systems/shop.ts:72 rolls tier 2/3 for any non-legendary pool item, including shortcut (price 12, shortcut.ts:7, no noShop) and binder (price 14). Tiered price = TIER.value, so a pricier star-2/3 offer with an identical effect is reachable in a real run.

Coin upgrade: upgradeItem (run.ts:241) is called only from src/buildlab/run.ts:76 and the bot (src/bot/bot.ts:392, weapons only). grep finds no caller in src/ui or src/scenes; ui/shop.ts imports mergeItems, upgradeShop, upgradeCart and upgradeShelf, not upgradeItem or upgradeCost. Only the shop-offer half holds: star-2/3 Shortcut Key and Binder offers cost 2-4x the base price for the same effect, and merging two copies wastes both. That is a wasted-coins trap, not a rule bug. findings.title: Buildlab proxy drops every hook-spawned shot, fire pool and beam echo, and does not list the affected combos as unmodelled. Ray Gun makes the Nail Gun deal 0 damage.
findings.location: src/engine/fakeCtx.ts:319-327 (spawnShot pushes to fake.playerShots, which nothing moves; spawnPool only logs), src/engine/fakeCtx.ts:337 (beam/sweep/explode only log), src/buildlab/combat.ts:454-455 (the step loop reads only dropCoin calls, then fake.clear()), src/buildlab/balance.ts:35-37 (UNMODELLED_COMBOS lists only the dash/pickup combos)
findings.scenario:
In the game, src/scenes/phaserCtx.ts:100-105 sends ctx.spawnShot to arsenal.spawn, ctx.spawnPool to spawnFirePool(arsenal, ...) and ctx.beam to beamOnce. In the buildlab, playAisle runs the same hooks on a FakeCtx. Its spawnShot puts the shot in fake.playerShots, which no code ever advances or collides. Its spawnPool and beam only append to fake.calls, and the buildlab loop discards those calls each step. FakeArsenal.spawn (fakeHost.ts) is a separate path and never sees them.

Repro, run in a throwaway vitest with playAisle, mode 'clear', 20 milk and hp 5000. Nail Gun alone: 312 dealt, 20 kills, cleared. Nail Gun + Battery + Magnet (Nailstorm): 345 dealt, cleared. Nail Gun + Battery + Tin Foil Hat + Magnet (Ray Gun): dealt=0, kills=0, cleared=false, bySource={}. The cause is that rayGun's 'pattern:fire' sets ev.handled = true and replaces the nail with a ctx.spawnShot bolt that never flies. Cooker + Tape (Shrapnel): 18 fragments spawned, 0 of them ever moved. Microwave + Fuel (Reheat): 4 pools spawned, and spawnPool only logs them, so they never burn.

Affected combos, all by the same mechanism: Ray Gun (the whole weapon goes silent), Shrapnel, Kettle Corn (spawnShot), Reheat, Pressure Point, Sizzling Skillet (spawnPool), and Power Surge's echo (beam). None of them is in UNMODELLED_COMBOS. The balance report therefore treats them as modelled ('Combos no top build formed', dominance and lift), and the fitness and greedy scoring reward forming them while the proxy gives them no payoff.

Impact today: the current buildlab-out/run.json mentions sizzlingSkillet 53 times, reheat 51 times and shrapnel 8 times. These Fuel and weapon combos do form, so their missing pool and fragment damage biases the current reports. The release checklist has Fuel in 88% of runs. Ray Gun is latent: its parts include passives, and the mechanics report shows that greedy placement never forms such combos. Once that placement artifact is fixed, Ray Gun will look like a trap in the proxy (it wipes out Nail Gun damage) while it is a strong combo in the game. docs/buildlab.md says the item hooks run on the FakeCtx and lists what is skipped. This gap is not in that list.
findings.fix: Connect the FakeCtx effect stubs to the FakeArsenal that playAisle builds. FakeArsenal implements PatternHost, so spawnFirePool(arsenal, ...), arsenal.spawn(...), and beamOnce, sweepOnce and explodeAt (as phaserCtx.ts:100-105 calls them) can all run against it. For example, give FakeCtx an optional host and forward spawnShot, spawnPool, beam, sweep and explode to it when one is set, then have playAisle set it to its arsenal. Until then, add rayGun, shrapnel, kettleCorn, reheat, pressurePoint, sizzlingSkillet and powerSurge to UNMODELLED_COMBOS, and mention the gap in docs/buildlab.md. Add a buildlab test asserting that a Ray Gun cart deals more than 0 damage.

findings.title: Punch Card never rolls in the buildlab proxy: its own effect is zero there, but the balance report treats it as modelled
findings.location: src/buildlab/combat.ts (no rollPunchCard, punchKill, punchTick or payPunchCard anywhere in src/buildlab), compared with src/scenes/ArenaScene.ts:194, 836, 1024 and 1081-1082; src/buildlab/balance.ts:29-34 (UNMODELLED does not list punchcard)
findings.scenario: The punchcard item has no build stats and no hooks (src/content/items/punchcard.ts). All of its value comes from ArenaScene: rollPunchCard at aisle start, progress through punchKill and punchTick, then payPunchCard for 5/8/12 coins plus the next shop's free reroll. playAisle in the buildlab never sets state.punch, so a Punch Card in the cart earns nothing in the proxy and only adds a Checkout set count. balance.ts flags an item as 'dead' only when it is modelled (`modelled = !(id in UNMODELLED)`). Punch Card can therefore be reported as a dead or weak item, and the economy curve the hillclimb tunes leaves out its coins. docs/buildlab.md's list of skipped features does not mention punch cards.
findings.fix: Roll the punch card at the start of playAisle, count kills and ticks with the shared punchKill and punchTick from systems/contracts, and call payPunchCard when the card is done. Otherwise, add `punchcard: 'aisle goal not simulated'` to UNMODELLED and mention it in docs/buildlab.md.

gaps.coverage:
Checked and found clean, no reports filed:

- **Audio** (src/audio/music.ts, sfx.ts):
  - Music crossfade and interval lifecycle; playMusic dedupe across ArenaScene restarts; shop-open → music_main.
  - SFX per-key voice counters: no stopAll, removeAll or stopByKey callers, so 'complete' always decrements.
